pages.text: Contexte - Journée des toilettes | Nations Unies Skip to main content UNICEF/Karel Prinsloo Qu’est-ce que la Journée mondiale des toilettes? La Journée mondiale des toilettes est organisée chaque année le 19 novembre afin d'encourager les actions en faveur de la réalisation de l’objectif de développement durable 6 (ODD 6): un accès universel à l’eau et à l’assainissement. Coordonnée par ONU-Eau, la Journée mondiale des toilettes est soutenue par des millions de personnes et d'institutions à travers le monde, qui diffusent des messages, organisent des événements et lancent des campagnes de sensibilisation. Pourquoi les toilettes sont-elles importantes ? L'accès à des services d’assainissement est un droit humain. Pourtant, des milliards d'êtres humains sont laissés pour compte, sans accès à des toilettes salubres, et en paient le prix fort, car cette situation a de lourdes conséquences pour leur santé, leur éducation, leurs moyens de subsistance et leur environnement. La crise planétaire de l'assainissement touche tout le monde, mais pas avec la même intensité. Ce sont les femmes, les filles et d'autres groupes vulnérables qui paient le plus lourd tribut. Que fait l'ONU pour contribuer à garantir l'accès universel à des toilettes sûres ? L’objectif de développement durable 6 est de garantir l'accès universel, d'ici 2030, à des services d'assainissement et d'hygiène gérés de manière sûre, «en accordant une attention particulière aux besoins des femmes, des filles et des personnes en situation de vulnérabilité». Copy markdown In this article About continuous integration Continuous integration (CI) is a software practice that requires frequently committing code to a shared repository. Committing code more often detects errors sooner and reduces the amount of code a developer needs to debug when finding the source of an error. Frequent code updates also make it easier to merge changes from different members of a software development team. This is great for developers, who can spend more time writing code and less time debugging errors or resolving merge conflicts. When you commit code to your repository, you can continuously build and test the code to make sure that the commit doesn't introduce errors. Your tests can include code linters (which check style formatting), security checks, code coverage, functional tests, and other custom checks. Building and testing your code requires a server. You can build and test updates locally before pushing code to a repository, or you can use a CI server that checks for new code commits in a repository. Introduction Ensuring only W3C representatives with appropriate approval and accountability are authorized to approve transactions is an important part of W3C Management's commitment to the responsible stewardship of W3C resources. Describe the issue below: Description: License: CC BY 4.0 arXiv:2611.00150v1 [astro-ph.IM] 30 Oct 2026 [orcid=0009-0009-4239-7070] [orcid=0000-0002-8178-8463] [orcid=0000-0002-2720-7218] Contrastive Astromer: Two-Stage Contrastive Representation Learning for Astronomical Light Curve Classification Justin Minggan Wei mwei@fas.harvard.edu Pavlos Protopapas Guillermo Cabrera-Vives organization=School of Engineering and Applied Sciences, Harvard University, city=Cambridge, state=MA, postcode=02138, country=USA organization=Department of Computer Science, Universidad de Concepción, addressline=Edmundo Larenas 219, city=Concepción, country=Chile Abstract Large astronomical surveys collect abundant light curves, but reliable class labels remain scarce. ASTROMER 2 learns from unlabeled light curves by reconstructing masked observations, yet this objective does not explicitly encourage class separation in a compact representation of each light curve. We introduce Contrastive Astromer, a two-stage approach that makes these representations more useful for classification without changing the ASTROMER 2 encoder architecture. First, unsupervised contrastive learning on single-band MACHO light curves brings together representations of augmented views of the same object. Supervised contrastive learning, supported by an auxiliary classification loss, then uses a separate labeled Alcock sample to strengthen class discrimination.

pages.text: Contratación equitativa | International Labour Organization Ir al contenido principal Portal temático Contratación equitativa Facebook X Linkedin © ILO En la actual economía globalizada, cada vez más los trabajadores emigran de su país con el fin de encontrar mejores oportunidades de empleo, en busca de un trabajo decente y mejores medios de vida. Además, millones de trabajadores emigran dentro de sus propios países en busca de trabajo decente. Las agencias de empleo públicas y privadas, cuando están debidamente reglamentadas, desempeñan un papel importante en el funcionamiento eficiente y equitativo de los mercados de trabajo, pues equiparan la oferta de empleo con trabajadores dotados de las calificaciones adecuadas. Sin embargo, se ha expresado preocupación por el papel cada vez más importante que desempeñan agencias de empleo sin escrúpulos, intermediarios del sector no estructurado de la mano de obra y otros operadores que actúan al margen del marco jurídico y reglamentario y que se dirigen en particular a los trabajadores poco calificados. Para responder a estos problemas, en 2014 se puso en marcha la "Iniciativa para la contratación equitativa" como parte del llamado del Director General de la OIT en pro de un Programa sobre la migración equitativa. A learning opportunity for those ready to dive deeper, even if you’re not in a sprint. pages.text: Contributing to the documentation — pandas 3.1.1 documentation Skip to main content Back to top Ctrl + K Choose version System Settings Light Dark GitHub X Mastodon Collapse Sidebar Expand Sidebar Contributing to the documentation # Contributing to the documentation benefits everyone who uses pandas. We encourage you to help us improve the documentation, and you don’t have to be an expert on pandas to do so! In fact, there are sections of the docs that are worse off after being written by experts. If something in the docs doesn’t make sense to you, updating the relevant section after you figure it out is a great way to ensure it will help the next person. Please visit the issues page for a full list of issues that are currently open regarding the pandas documentation. Share sensitive information only on official, secure websites. https://www.nist.gov/publications/conversion-reported-temperatures-historical-scales-its-90 PUBLICATIONS Conversion of Reported Temperatures from Historical Scales to the ITS-90 Published October 26, 2026 Author(s) Allan Harvey Abstract While the International Temperature Scale of 1990 (ITS-90) has been a standard for many years, there is a large amount of historical thermophysical data reported on other scales. The differences of these scales from ITS-90 is typically small, but not necessarily negligible for reference-quality work. We describe conversion to ITS-90 from 34 different scales. These include not only the relatively well-known International Temperature Scales from 1968, 1948, and 1927, but also scales that have been used for cryogenic work at temperatures below the ranges of the older international scales, including the many scales that were based on the vapor pressure of helium. Scales specific to certain laboratories are also considered. Python code has been made available for the conversions described here. Cooperative Agriculture Opportunities Updated September 21, 2026 Cooperative agriculture — partnering with farmers and ranchers to meet wildlife management objectives — is a long-standing practice on national wildlife refuges ( 50 CFR 29.2 ). Cooperative agreements between the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service and farmers or ranchers may permit grazing by cattle or the growing of grain, hay or other crops at a refuge. The refuge benefits by producing food for wildlife or by improving natural habitat. The farmer profits by harvesting and selling some of the crop. The rancher gains access to grazing land. Cooperative agriculture is used on refuges only in situations where the Fish and Wildlife Service cannot meet its resource management objectives through the maintenance, management or mimicking of natural ecosystem processes or functions. How to Apply Cooperative agriculture agreements on refuges are awarded through an open and competitive process. Warming of the atmosphere, oceans and land – driven by human activity – is causing climate variations and extremes all over the world, with over three billion people living in places that are highly vulnerable to climate change (IPCC, 2023). Action taken to date by the international community has been insufficient to prevent or reverse these trends. Share Share on X Share on LinkedIn Share on Facebook The negative effects of climate change are being felt in some of the most extreme ways by people living in places affected by armed conflict and other violence, who are ill-equipped to cope with and adapt to a changing climate and receive inadequate support to that end (ICRC, 2020 and 2023). Over the last few years, there has been increased recognition of the urgent need to strengthen climate action in places enduring armed conflict and other fragile settings, as reflected in the COP28 Declaration on Climate, Relief, Recovery and Peace. This article is more than 2 years old With $1tn a year needed, we analyse how best to fill the gap, from wealth taxes to levies on flying and oil extraction Fiona Harvey Environment editor Mon 11 Nov 2024 04.00 EST Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Countries meeting in Baku, Azerbaijan, for the Cop29 climate summit are under pressure to find ways to raise money to help poorer nations cut greenhouse gas emissions, shift to a low-carbon economy, and adapt to the impacts of extreme weather. At least $1tn a year is needed. Developed countries are willing to ensure about half of that is provided from public sources, leaving a large gap that countries are hoping to fill with other sources of cash, known as innovative forms of finance .
